title: Infinite series of Deza graphs with strongly regular children
summary: A Deza graph is a regular graph in which the number of common neighbours of two distinct vertices takes at most two values, regardless of adjacency. Its children are the graphs on the same vertex set in which adjacency is determined by these two common-neighbour counts. A Deza graph is called strongly Deza if both children are strongly regular. We construct an infinite family of edge-regular strongly Deza graphs using non-degenerate quadratic forms over the field with five elements.
